**Planner warning: Sunbelt Charter Coaches — large-group shuttle failure**

I’m posting this because I know a lot of us use Sunbelt for airport transfers and offsite transportation, and I’d want the facts before booking them for CES.

For a client dinner on Thursday, Nov. 5, I booked four coaches for 220 people. Pickup was scheduled for 6:15 p.m. at our hotel, with transportation to a ranch venue in Henderson. The booking was confirmed in writing twice, most recently Tuesday, Nov. 3. Total cost was $8,400: a 50% deposit in September and the balance seven days before the event. Corey was the dispatcher listed throughout.

Only two coaches arrived. The first was 55 minutes late, and the driver told me he had received the job at 5 p.m. The second broke down on the 215. Its air conditioning was out, and passengers were stuck on the shoulder for roughly 40 minutes. The other two coaches never arrived.

With no backup plan or communication from dispatch, I put about 60 attendees into Ubers and Lyfts on my company card. Those rides cost approximately $1,900. Dinner started at 8:40 p.m. instead of 7 p.m., and our caterer charged us overtime.

The office line has gone to voicemail since Friday, and I’m still waiting for a resolution. I’m seeking a refund for the two coaches that never came, plus reimbursement of the rideshare costs.

To be fair, Sunbelt handled two small airport runs for me last spring and did a great job, which is why I trusted them with this event. One late bus would have been manageable. Having no contingency plan and no communication during a 220-person event is not.

My client is now reviewing whether to keep my company for its March event, so this has had consequences well beyond one difficult night.

My advice to other planners is simple: don’t book Sunbelt for anything large or time-sensitive until they demonstrate that dispatch, backup planning, and customer communication have been fixed. I’ll update this post if they resolve the refund.
